name: P*TIME
tagline: Korean in-memory OLTP engine acquired by SAP in 2005; its technology fed into SAP HANA.
description: P*TIME was a main-memory relational OLTP engine that grew out of Sang Kyun Cha's research group at Seoul National University and was commercialised by Transact In Memory, Inc.; a VLDB 2004 industrial paper presented it as a highly scalable DBMS for update-intensive stream workloads. Its design leaned on ideas from the same group, notably latch-free optimistic index traversal and differential logging, which allows logging and recovery to run in parallel, to scale on multiprocessors at a time when most engines were disk-bound. SAP acquired the company in 2005, and P*TIME became one of the building blocks of SAP HANA alongside the TREX column engine and MaxDB's liveCache. It was never sold standalone under SAP; use SAP HANA or another in-memory OLTP engine today.
statusNote: Transact In Memory was acquired by SAP in 2005; P*TIME was absorbed into SAP HANA and is not sold separately.
developer: Transact In Memory, Inc. (acquired by SAP)

pricing.notes: Not sold since the 2005 SAP acquisition.

scale.notes: Single-node main-memory engine optimised for multiprocessor scalability.

strengths: Early demonstration of multicore-scalable in-memory OLTP
Parallel logging and recovery via differential logging
Direct ancestor of parts of SAP HANA
weaknesses: Never available outside its short commercial life before SAP
Little public documentation beyond research papers
useCases: Studying the origins of SAP HANA
Background reading on latch-free in-memory OLTP design
notIdealFor: Any deployment: the product no longer exists
